[[Private banking]] | parent = [[Bank of Baroda]], [[Ministry of Finance (India)|Ministry of Finance]], [[Government of India]] | revenue = {{increase}}{{INRConvert|751.85|c}} (2025)[http://www.nainitalbank.bank.in/pdf/Fin_results_2017.pdf "Balance Sheet 31.03.2017"]. nainitalbank.bank.in (15 March 2018). | operating_income = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|89.02 |c}} (2025) | net_income = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|50.61|c}} (2025) | assets = {{increase}}{{INRConvert|9360.48|c}} (2025) | equity = | ratio = | num_employees = 1188 | founded = 1922 | hq_location = [[Nainital]], [[Uttarakhand]], India | branches = | website = {{URL|www.nainitalbank.bank.in}} }} '''The Nainital Bank Limited''' (NTB) (known as '''Nainital Bank'''){{cite web|url=http://www.nainitalbank.bank.in |title=Nainital Bank}} is a scheduled commercial bank founded in 1922. The bank is a [[subsidiary]] of [[Bank of Baroda]] which is under the [[ownership]] of [[Ministry of Finance (India)|Ministry of Finance]] of the [[Government of India]]. The bank has expanded to [[Uttar Pradesh]],[[Uttarakhand]], [[Rajasthan]], [[Delhi]] and [[Haryana]] and has 173 branches.{{cite web|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/Views/Recommendations/articleshow/5985388.cms |title=Growth potential for Bank of Baroda is pretty high: Arihant Capital Markets|work=[[The Economic Times]]|date=28 May 2010 |access-date=20 August 2010}} ==Overview== Nainital Bank was founded by [[Govind Ballabh Pant]].{{cite news |title=BoB to merge its associate bank |url=http://www.financialexpress.com/news/bob-to-merge-its-associate-bank/172293/0 |work=[[The Financial Express (India)|The Financial Express]] |date=25 July 2006 }} In 1922, the government-owned [[Bank of Baroda]] (BOB), the second largest bank in India, acquired a 98.6% (around 99%) stake in the bank and made it a subsidiary.{{cite web |title=Domestic: Subsidiary |url=http://www.bankofbaroda.com/subsidiaries_jv.asp |publisher= [[Bank of Baroda]] }} The bank had a net worth of around Rs 8.37  billion on as on 31 March 2025.{{cite news |title=Banks struggle with RBI norms|url=http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2006-10-01/india-business/27804597_1_ratnakar-bank-centrum-finance-sangli-bank |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120927184850/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2006-10-01/india-business/27804597_1_ratnakar-bank-centrum-finance-sangli-bank |url-status=dead |archive-date=27 September 2012 |work=[[The Times of India]]|date=1 October 2006 }} It bank launched its [[rights issue]] in September 2009, to expand its [[capital adequacy ratio]] (CAR) to 14 per cent, this came after it previously withdrew its plans for an [[Initial public offering|IPO]] due to adverse market conditions in 2007; by April 2010, the right issue had raised {{INRConvert|300|m}}.{{cite news |title=Nainital Bank drops plan for public issue |url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2007-06-21/news/28436108_1_public-issue-parent-bank-private-bank |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120527150124/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2007-06-21/news/28436108_1_public-issue-parent-bank-private-bank |url-status=dead |archive-date=27 May 2012 |work=[[The Economic Times]] |date=21 June 2007 }}{{cite news |title=Nainital Bank raises Rs 30 cr.|url=http://www.business-standard.com/power/news/nainital-bank-raises-rs-30-cr/12/05/390349/ |work=[[Business Standard]]|location=India |date=1 April 2010}} Nainital bank is associated with [[Bank of Baroda]], Currently, NBL has 173 branches in Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana and Rajasthan. It also provide online facilities, apart from Personal Banking, Business Banking, Rural and Agricultural Banking. The Nainital Bank Limited is registered as scheduled commercial bank with [[Reserve Bank of India]] (RBI), the [[central bank]] of India..{{cite web|url=http://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/AboutUsDisplay.aspx?pg=Indian.htm |title= RBI Private Bank-Indian Bank|publisher=[[Reserve Bank of India]]}}{{cite book |title=The Great Deleveraging: Economic Growth and Investing Strategies for the Future|chapter=List of Banks in India (2009)|author= Chip Dickson|author2=Oded Shenkar|publisher=FT Press|year= 2009|isbn=978-0-13-235810-1 |page=[https://archive.org/details/greatdeleveragin0000dick/page/217 217] |url=https://archive.org/details/greatdeleveragin0000dick |url-access=registration|quote=Nainital Bank.|ref=Di }} In December 2024, Nainital Bank upgraded its RTGS, NEFT, and net-banking systems to comply with RBI and IFTAS guidelines, aiming to provide customers with faster, more secure, and seamless online fund transfer services using advanced encryption technologies.{{Cite web |date=2024-12-14 |title=Nainital Bank's fund transfer technologies updated - extract: The Nainital Bank Limited (NTB) (known as Nainital Bank) is a scheduled commercial bank founded in 1922. The bank is a subsidiary of Bank of Baroda which is under the ownership of Ministry of Finance of the Government of India. The bank has expanded to Uttar Pradesh,Uttarakhand, Rajasthan, Delhi and Haryana  and has 173 branches.
